title: Sharpen a knife in a pull-through sharpener: hold it, coarse then fine, pull only
instruction: Sharpen the chef's knife with the pull-through sharpener, then put the knife back in its dock.
context: Pull-through sharpener instructions describe a fixed procedure. Etch Couteaux: hold the sharpener's handle firmly with one hand so it cannot slip, pull the knife toward you heel to tip in the coarse slot, then the fine slot, never back and forth. The item 191H manual: blade vertical; the No. 1 coarse slot sets the edge, the No. 2 fine slot hones it; always pull heel to tip. Smith's directions add moderate downward pressure; the KitchenKnives.com guide gives 3-5 passes per slot. The instruction only says to sharpen the knife and put it back, so the task checks the procedure unprompted. Two arms by friction: the 100 g sharpener stands on slippery feet on a wet board while its slot grips the blade; in the recorded one-arm variant it slid 15.32 cm with the knife and no pass counted (score 0); held, it moved 1.09-1.25 cm per pass. Done by: cooks and home cooks.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Knife dock: dark wood, fixed, 23 cm long (along x) and 5 cm wide, centred at x 41, y -24 (it runs from x 29.5 to 52.5), with a V-groove along its top whose floor is 5 cm above the table (the groove is 1.2 cm deep, 0.4 cm wide at its floor and 1.6 cm at its top). Chef's knife: 0.20 kg, standing edge-down in the groove with its point away from the robot and its handle toward the robot; the heel of the edge rests on the groove's floor at x 30, y -24. Steel blade 2 mm thick and 4.5 cm high; the edge is 20.8 cm long, straight for 15 cm and then rising 3 cm over the last 5 cm to the point; a steel bolster 2 cm long; a black hollow handle 10.5 cm long, 1.6 cm thick and 2.4 cm high (32.5 cm long in all, from x 17.5 to 50). Cutting board: white plastic, wet, fixed, 24 x 34 x 1.5 cm, centred at x 36, y 0. Pull-through sharpener: 0.10 kg, a blue body 6 x 22 x 2 cm (long side along y) on four black feet 0.4 cm high, centred at x 40, y 0 on the board; a handle 3.5 x 8 x 3.5 cm on top of its left end (centred at y 6.5); two slots running front to back (along x), each 5 cm long and centred at x 40: the coarse carbide slot (dark) at y -3.5 and the fine ceramic slot (white) at y -7.5. Each slot is a V-groove 1.8 cm deep, 0.4 cm wide at its floor and 1.4 cm at its top, in a housing 3.4 cm wide; the slot floor (the abrasive) is 2.4 cm above the board, 3.9 cm above the table.
scoring: Every step, from poses and the knife-on-sharpener contact force; the score at the end counts. The blade is in a slot when it lies along the slot and upright (each within about 20 degrees, cosine 0.94), the middle of the slot meets the edge between 1 cm behind the heel and the point, and there the edge is inside the slot (within its 1.4 cm wide top opening and no higher than its top). A pass is one contact: it starts when the blade is in a slot with a contact force of at least 0.5 N and ends after more than 3 steps off the abrasive or when the blade moves to the other slot. A pass is valid when the point where the slot's middle meets the edge travels at least 12 cm from heel toward tip over the steps pressed at 1.5 N or more, at least 80% of the pass's touching steps are pressed, it has no more than 1 cm of backward (tip-to-heel) travel, and the sharpener moves no more than 2 cm horizontally during it. Valid coarse passes count; valid fine passes count only after three valid coarse passes (earlier ones are recorded and do not count). Score: 1/6 per counted coarse pass and per counted fine pass, up to three of each, capped at 0.75 while the knife is not back in its dock. The knife is in its dock when its heel is within the first 8 cm of the groove from the dock's near end, within 0.8 cm of the groove's centre line and no more than 6 mm above its floor, the blade within 30 degrees of upright, its point within 15 degrees of straight away from the robot, and no finger pad within 1 cm of its handle. 1.0 (success): three counted passes in each slot and the knife in its dock. 0 from the moment of sawing (more than 2 cm of tip-to-heel travel in one contact), any finger pad of the left (holding) hand within 1.5 cm of a slot housing, the sharpener tipped more than 20 degrees, or the knife dropped (its heel falls 3 cm within 10 steps while no finger pad is within 2 cm of its handle).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the knife back in its dock, edge down with its point away from the robot, and put the sharpener back in the middle of the board with its handle on the left. For real trials, wet the board again; each real pass removes a little steel from the blade.
fidelity: Rigid boxes (knife; sharpener feet, body, handle and slots; fixed board and dock). The knife-on-sharpener contact force is read each step. Abrasion is not simulated (the strips are visual, the edge does not change), so passes are counted as the instructions describe: pressed, heel to tip over at least 12 cm, never back, coarse before fine, sharpener held still. The wet board is friction 0.05 under feet of 0.10. A 1.5 cm finger keep-out from the slots stands in for the blade's path.
